posts.post_subject: Beamsplitter for H1 to H2 copy.
posts.content_md:
Hi, Im thinking of buying a BS. Can anyone tell me if the cheaper of these will be ok, or should I go for the more expensive cube, they are both from [http://www.surplusshed.com/](http://www.surplusshed.com/) they have the following descriptions:

1. MIRROR TYPE GLASS BEAMSPLITTER, 50MM SQ 

Beamspitter appears to be 25% transmittance and 75% reflective. 50mm long x 50mm wide. Unused.

Item No: M3014

Price: $2.50 

2. 15MM COATED CUBE BEAMSPLITTER 

Unused beauty in original packaging. 15mm X 15mm cube beamsplitter. Transmission and reflection is in the ratio of 50/50. Made of BK7 with surface quality 60/40. Angle tolerance is +- 3 arc min and flatness is 1/2 wave. All sides are antireflection coated. Edmund's 15mm X 15mm sells for $118.80

Item No: L2046D

Price: $19.00 

They are for use with the 3mw Integraf laser.

Thanks, Rick.

posts.topic_title: Beamsplitter for H1 to H2 copy.
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Beamsplitter for H1 to H2 copy.
posts.content_md: You will do better with the mirrored one for H1 to H2 because of the ratios needed. You might even be able to get away with a piece of glass as a 90/10 beam splitter. You will be surprised how much light you need to send to the H1 to get your beam ratios correct.

The surplusshed cubes work OK, but I haven't used mine for H1/H2 work. I've been looking for a variable filter, but so far I haven't found one that suits my budget yet. I don't have as deep pockets as some people.

--Ted.
